chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from al-Khayari, from al-Husayn ibn Thuwair, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When hunger strikes you, play with (or eat slowly) the raisins.

key_terms.فَاعْبَثُوا: Play with / eat slowly / consume leisurely

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended way to handle hunger according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises consuming raisins during times of famine, where the term 'abatha' (to play with or toss about) suggests either eating them slowly to prolong satiety or using them as a light snack to curb hunger pangs. This guidance highlights the practical wisdom of utilizing accessible, energy-dense foods like raisins for immediate relief and reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preventative health measures rooted in daily life. The advice underscores the importance of moderation and resourcefulness in managing sustenance, particularly in times of scarcity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Al Khayri, from Al Husayn Bin Suweyr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When hunger hits you, so play with (eat slowly) the raisins’.
en.sarwar: 18. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il ibn Bazi’ from al-Khaybariy from al-Husayn ibn Thuwayri who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When you are hungry play (eat slowly) with raisins.
